note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Both statewide races are open seats with the primary on Aug 18, 2026: Sen. Lummis is retiring and Gov. Gordon is not seeking a third term.

WY-senate.statusNote: Open seat, Sen. Cynthia Lummis is retiring. Rep. Harriet Hageman (R) and former state Rep. James Byrd (D) won their Aug 18 primaries.

WY-governor.statusNote: Open seat, Gov. Mark Gordon is not seeking a third term. State Sen. Eric Barlow (R) defeated Megan Degenfelder in the Aug 18 primary. Kenneth Casner (D) won the Democratic nomination. Rebecca Bextel of Jackson (Constitution Party) is also on the November ballot.

WY-house-at-large.statusNote: Secretary of State Chuck Gray (R) won a crowded nine-way August 18, 2026 Republican primary to succeed Harriet Hageman, who ran for Senate instead; Lisa Kinney won the Democratic primary; Constitution nominee Jeff Haggit, Libertarian nominee Shawn Johnson, and independent Daniel Workman also qualified for the November ballot (The Green Papers Wyoming 2026 general candidate roster; WyoFile). Positions researched and stored, race not scored, overlap 0 of 10 as of Sep 2, 2026.

candidates.name: Harriet Hageman
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for Wyoming's at-large district since 2023; trial and natural resources attorney who grew up on a ranch near Fort Laramie. She unseated Rep. Liz Cheney in the 2022 primary. Running for the open Senate seat with endorsements from President Trump, Sen. Barrasso and retiring Sen. Lummis.
priorities: Legacy energy: coal, oil, gas and uranium
Reining in federal spending and overreach

housing.label: Backed the 2025 budget provision selling 'small, underutilized parcels near towns' of federal land for housing and economic growth (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Voted for H.R. 2, the Secure the Border Act, passed 219-213 (House roll call 209, 2023)

taxes.label: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, permanently extending the 2017 tax cuts, passed 218-214 (House roll call 190, 2025)

climate.label: 'America is blessed with abundant natural resources which can ensure that we have accessible and affordable energy'; names coal, oil, gas and uranium as legacy sources that can meet demand (House issues page)

repro.label: Voted for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act, H.R. 26, passed 220-210 (House roll call 29, 2023)

democracy.label: Voted for the SAVE Act requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote, passed 220-208 (House roll call 102, 2025)

education.label: Voted for H.R. 5, the Parental Bill of Rights Act: 'Parents have every right to know what their children are being taught' (hageman.house.gov)

candidates.name: James Byrd
candidates.background: Former Wyoming state representative from Cheyenne (2009-2019) who served as House Minority Whip; fifth-generation Wyomingite and son of trailblazing legislator Liz Byrd. Worked as an exploration geophysicist for energy firms and as an IT project manager for American Express and Cargill; 2018 Democratic nominee for Secretary of State.
priorities: Rural healthcare access and drug cost caps

health.label: Prescription drug cost caps, permanent telehealth reimbursements, transparent medical pricing and protecting rural hospital infrastructure (WyoFile election guide)

immigration.label: Mixed: 'we must secure our borders and enforce the rule of law', while a framework must balance 'strict border security with humanitarian values'; modernize visas for agriculture, ranching and hospitality (WyoFile election guide)

climate.label: Mixed: 'I love coal. I am not against fossil fuel industry', yet says Wyoming must diversify beyond fossil fuels and own emerging energy technologies (Cowboy State Daily)

candidates.name: Megan Degenfelder
candidates.background: Wyoming Superintendent of Public Instruction since 2023; sixth-generation Wyomingite from Casper who spent nearly a decade in government affairs for coal, oil and gas companies and once staffed then-Rep. Cynthia Lummis. Cancer survivor and rugby coach. Endorsed by President Trump, who calls her 'MAGA Megan', and by Rep. Harriet Hageman.
priorities: Wyoming energy dominance and local control of lands

cost.label: 'The government doesn't create jobs, the private sector does': eliminate regulations, though data centers 'cannot build here if you will increase rates for residents' (WyoFile election guide)

taxes.label: Property tax relief and reducing nonessential spending while leveraging energy revenue to fund essential services (WyoFile election guide)

climate.label: Prioritizes Wyoming 'energy dominance', protecting grazing, energy and timber development; nearly a decade in coal, oil and gas regulatory affairs (WyoFile election guide)

education.label: Supported legislation authorizing charter schools and a voucher program for private tuition; as superintendent pushed a legislative agenda to cement school choice and expand parental control (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Opposes any exceptions to abortion bans: 'I can't accept any exception when it comes to life' (WyoFile)

candidates.name: Eric Barlow
candidates.now: Wyoming State Senator; chair, Senate Labor, Health and Social Services Committee
candidates.background: Wyoming state senator from Gillette and former Speaker of the House (2021-2022); Marine Corps veteran, large-animal veterinarian and Campbell County rancher. The Wyoming Freedom Caucus chair attacks him as 'a liberal Republican who loves big government.' His campaign released a July 2026 internal poll showing him at 42% to Degenfelder's 19%, which her campaign disputes.
priorities: Rural healthcare access via a 'healthcare strike team'
Public lands access and private property rights

taxes.label: Cash-based budgeting, 'right-sized government' and maintaining state savings to keep taxes lower (WyoFile election guide)

climate.label: Co-sponsored House Bill 75, the 2025 law cutting Wyoming's severance tax on surface-mined coal from 6.5% to 6% (WyoFile)

safety.label: Led 2023 law expanding rights restoration, including jury service, for first-time nonviolent felony convictions (WyoFile)

repro.label: Supported a near-total abortion ban and a medication abortion ban in 2023 (WyoFile)

education.label: Co-sponsored the 2024 $6,000 education savings account bill but voted no on final passage after 31 amendments (WyoFile)

candidates.name: Kenneth Casner
candidates.background: Elk Mountain Democrat making his third run for governor after campaigns in 2002 and 2018, and the only Democrat in the 2026 race. Accepts no campaign donations and says 'I'm fighting for Wyoming now. I want to leave her in better shape than what she is today.' He did not respond to WyoFile's candidate questionnaire.

taxes.label: Supports implementing a Wyoming state income tax (Wyoming Public Media)

education.label: Supports public school funding and focusing on history education in public schools (Wyoming Public Media)

candidates.name: Chuck Gray
candidates.background: Wyoming Secretary of State since 2023 and former state representative, won the crowded August 18, 2026 Republican primary to succeed Harriet Hageman (who ran for Senate instead).

cost.label: Advocates reducing 'inflation through reductions in the debt and deficit' and rolling back federal regulations to lower living costs (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

health.label: Calls the Affordable Care Act 'one of the worst things to happen to our country,' backs selling 'insurance across state lines' and price-disclosure requirements (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

immigration.label: 'I 100% support President Trump's approach to stopping illegal immigration,' backing completion of the border wall and a sanctuary-city ban (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

climate.label: Describes himself as 'a fierce defender of Wyoming's energy economy' committed to protecting coal, oil, gas and soda ash, and rolling back environmental regulations (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

democracy.label: As Secretary of State, led Wyoming to become 'the first state in the nation to require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote' and banned ranked-choice voting (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

candidates.name: Lisa Kinney
candidates.background: Former Wyoming state senator and attorney, first Wyoming Democrat to announce a run for the seat; won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary.

health.label: Backs restoring ACA subsidies and forming 'a bigger pool' of Western states to cut premiums, plus 'affordable health care, reduced cost of prescription drugs, and accessibility for all' (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

housing.label: Proposes federal land transfers to cities for housing development via 'federal documents to transfer lands to the city' rather than selling public land wholesale (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

immigration.label: 'Congress needs to write laws to include some immigrants, and exclude the dangerous ones,' with protections for DACA recipients and Dreamers (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

education.label: Supports reinstating 'the Department of Education for some services,' particularly on tribal lands (WyoFile 2026 Election Guide)

nullNotes.cost: checked WyoFile 2026 Election Guide profile; her 'eliminating income tax for those earning under $100,000 and reducing FICA' proposal is a tax-policy item, not a prices/markets stance, so it does not fit this axis (checked Sep 2, 2026)
